questions.question: A retail website runs on EC2 instances behind an ALB. Server load surges without warning during flash sales and sits nearly idle overnight. The operations team wants to eliminate overnight idle costs while absorbing unpredictable sales spikes without manual intervention. Which compute strategy achieves this?
options: Run a fixed fleet at peak size using Reserved Instances to lower hourly cost
Configure an Auto Scaling Group with a CPU target tracking policy at 60%
Pre-scale with Scheduled Scaling set to business hours on weekdays
Migrate to Spot Instances across the fleet to reduce baseline cost
questions.explanation: Target tracking auto-scaling dynamically adjusts fleet size to keep average CPU near the target, shrinking the fleet overnight to cut idle spend and adding instances as sales traffic surges — no manual intervention required. Option C (Scheduled Scaling) fires on a calendar trigger; flash sales that arrive outside the configured window will overwhelm an under-provisioned fleet, so it does not handle genuinely unpredictable spikes. Spot Instances reduce per-hour pricing but can be reclaimed by AWS with two minutes' notice at peak demand, creating unacceptable availability risk for a customer-facing retail site.

questions.question: An online gaming platform stores a real-time leaderboard mapping player IDs to scores and ranks. During peak tournament events, the service handles 600,000 read operations per minute and every lookup is by a single player ID — no aggregations or joins are required. Response latency must stay under 5 milliseconds as player count is expected to triple over the next year. Which AWS database service is the best fit?
options: Amazon Aurora MySQL with a Multi-AZ standby and provisioned IOPS
Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity mode
Amazon Redshift with result-set caching enabled for repeated queries
Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached used as the authoritative data store
questions.explanation: DynamoDB is purpose-built for high-throughput, low-latency key lookups at any scale — on-demand capacity automatically adjusts to handle unpredictable peak volumes without manual provisioning, and single-digit millisecond performance is maintained regardless of table size. Aurora MySQL is a relational engine optimized for transactional workloads with complex queries; matching DynamoDB's sub-5ms key-lookup latency at 600k requests/minute requires significant tuning overhead and dedicated read replicas, making it a poor fit for this simple, high-volume access pattern. Memcached (option D) is an in-memory cache without durability — all data is lost on node restart or eviction, making it unsuitable as the authoritative store for a leaderboard that must persist through failures.

questions.question: An application stores user-uploaded files in S3. Files are frequently accessed for the first 30 days, rarely accessed for the next 60 days, then never needed again. Which S3 lifecycle configuration minimizes storage cost?
options: S3 Standard with no lifecycle policy, retaining objects indefinitely
Transition to S3 Standard-IA at day 30; expire at 90 days total
Store all objects in S3 Glacier Deep Archive from day 1 of upload
Apply S3 Intelligent-Tiering to manage storage class automatically
questions.explanation: S3 Standard-IA charges lower per-GB storage rates than Standard but adds a per-GB retrieval fee — an ideal trade-off once objects transition from frequent to infrequent access after day 30. Expiring objects at day 90 (30 active + 60 infrequent = 90 total) eliminates any ongoing cost for data that will never be needed again. Option C (Glacier Deep Archive from day 1) imposes up to 12-hour retrieval delays during the first 30 days when files are frequently accessed, making retrieval fees and latency far worse than the storage savings during that initial window.

questions.question: An e-commerce site runs EC2 instances behind an ALB, with all instances in a single subnet in us-east-1a. During an AWS maintenance event affecting that Availability Zone, the application returns 503 errors for 40 minutes. The architecture team must ensure no future single-AZ event causes a full outage. What change addresses the root cause?
options: Reduce the ALB health check interval to 5 s and enable EC2 Auto Recovery on each instance
Enable a second AZ on the ALB and deploy instances in us-east-1b
Schedule AMI snapshots hourly and restore into us-east-1b when outages occur
Create a second Region failover stack in us-west-2 using Route 53 health checks
questions.explanation: Deploying instances across two Availability Zones and enabling both AZs on the ALB ensures the load balancer continues routing traffic to healthy instances in the surviving AZ when the other AZ is impaired — the minimum change to remove the single-AZ dependency. Option A (EC2 Auto Recovery) restarts a failed instance on healthy hardware within the same Availability Zone; it protects against individual hardware failure but cannot mitigate an event that impairs the entire AZ. Option C (AMI snapshots with manual restore) requires operator action during the outage window, making recovery time unpredictable and far longer than an automated multi-AZ design.

questions.question: A DevOps engineer discovers that an EC2 web application is calling S3 using access keys stored in a plaintext configuration file on the instance. The security team requires these long-lived credentials to be removed immediately while preserving S3 read access. What should the solutions architect recommend?
options: Rotate the access keys and redeploy the application with updated credential values
Store the credentials as SecureString parameters in AWS Systems Manager
Attach an IAM role to the instance and remove all hard-coded access keys
Create a dedicated IAM user and reference credentials through environment variables
questions.explanation: Attaching an IAM role to an EC2 instance causes the instance metadata service (IMDS) to vend temporary, automatically-rotated credentials — no static keys exist to be stolen or leaked. The application calls S3 using the same SDK calls with no code changes required. Option D still uses long-lived IAM user credentials stored on disk, which carries the same fundamental risk as the original config file; it improves secret discoverability but does not eliminate the static-credential exposure.

questions.question: A SaaS company's CRM application uses Amazon RDS MySQL as its primary database. A newly deployed analytics dashboard runs complex GROUP BY queries across three years of interaction records, pushing primary instance CPU to 90% during business hours and causing response time degradation for transactional users. Writes must continue on the primary without interruption. Which solution isolates the analytics workload without affecting transactional performance?
options: Route analytics queries to the Multi-AZ standby via its read-only endpoint and connection string
Add an RDS Read Replica and direct the analytics dashboard to its endpoint
Enable RDS Performance Insights and configure automatic query termination for slow statements
Upgrade the primary instance to the next larger size tier to absorb both workloads
questions.explanation: An RDS Read Replica receives asynchronous replication from the primary and exposes a separate endpoint — heavy analytics queries run against the replica, leaving primary CPU available for transactional writes. The Multi-AZ standby in option A is a synchronous failover replica maintained solely for high availability; it does not accept query traffic and has no addressable read endpoint, so routing analytics connections to it is not supported by RDS. Upgrading the primary instance class (option D) reduces per-query CPU headroom but does not isolate the workloads — a 40-second analytics scan still competes with transactional queries for shared CPU and I/O, and the benefit erodes as data volume grows.

questions.question: A startup's production environment has web servers in public subnets and application servers in private subnets. After migrating to a newly created VPC, the application servers can no longer download software patches from the internet, although they receive no inbound connections. What change should the solutions architect make?
options: Update the private subnet route table to forward all 0.0.0.0/0 traffic to the existing Internet Gateway
Deploy a NAT Gateway in the public subnet and update the private subnet route table
Allocate an Elastic IP to each application server in the private subnet
Add a VPC peering connection to a transit VPC that has internet access
questions.explanation: A NAT Gateway placed in a public subnet uses the subnet's Internet Gateway to make outbound connections on behalf of private-subnet resources, translating source addresses so replies route back correctly. Private instances initiate the connection but remain unreachable from the internet because they have no public IP and no inbound route. Option A would fail because private-subnet instances lack public IPs — routing their traffic directly to the Internet Gateway causes packets to be dropped since there is no valid public-to-private address mapping.

questions.question: A global software vendor needs to publish product documentation, images, and downloadable PDFs for a product launch microsite. The 3 GB file set is updated roughly once per month and must load quickly for visitors across North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific. The team has no dedicated server administrators and must minimize both cost and ongoing operational effort. Which architecture meets these requirements?
options: Deploy file-serving EC2 instances in three regions behind Route 53 latency-based routing with Auto Scaling
Host the assets in S3 and distribute them through a CloudFront distribution with edge caching
Use Elastic Beanstalk to run a Node.js server that reads assets from an Amazon EFS volume
Place files in S3 and expose them through an Application Load Balancer with cross-zone load balancing enabled
questions.explanation: S3 provides durable, serverless object storage with no servers to patch or scale, and CloudFront distributes content from 400+ edge locations so visitors worldwide receive files from the nearest point of presence — achieving sub-100ms load times with no compute to operate. Multi-region EC2 in option A achieves geographic proximity but requires capacity planning, OS patching, Auto Scaling configuration, and 24/7 operations in each region, directly violating the 'no dedicated administrators' constraint. An Application Load Balancer (option D) cannot use S3 as a native origin, does not perform edge caching, and would still require backend compute to serve the files.

questions.question: A security audit finds that a Lambda function processing payment records connects to an RDS PostgreSQL database using the publicly accessible endpoint. The security team requires the database to be unreachable from the internet while Lambda retains the ability to execute queries. What configuration achieves this?
options: Deploy Lambda inside the VPC and configure the RDS security group to allow access from the Lambda SG
Remove RDS public access and restrict connections via RDS resource-based policies scoped to Lambda's execution role
Keep RDS publicly accessible and rotate database credentials hourly using Secrets Manager
Create a VPC peering connection to route Lambda traffic into the private RDS subnet
questions.explanation: Configuring Lambda with VPC settings creates an ENI in the specified subnets, allowing Lambda to reach RDS over private IP addresses — no public endpoint required. Disabling RDS public accessibility ensures no internet-originating connection can reach the database. Option B is incorrect because RDS does not support resource-based policies that restrict TCP-level connectivity; network access is controlled by security groups, not by a role-scoped policy attached to the RDS resource itself.

questions.question: An e-commerce platform's order service publishes completed orders to three independent downstream systems — inventory management, shipping fulfillment, and customer email — each of which must process every order event. The engineering team requires that adding a new consumer needs no changes to the order service. Which AWS pattern achieves this?
options: Publish to an SNS topic; each service subscribes via its own SQS queue
Route orders to a Kinesis Data Stream; each downstream service reads from a dedicated shard
Write directly to each downstream service's individual SQS queue from the order service
Store orders in DynamoDB Streams and configure each consumer to react to item changes
questions.explanation: The SNS fan-out pattern decouples the producer from consumers completely — the order service publishes once to a topic, and each SQS-subscribed service receives an independent copy automatically. Adding a new consumer requires only a new SNS subscription, with zero changes to the order service. Option C (writing directly to each SQS queue) creates N point-to-point dependencies — when a new consumer is added, the order service code must be updated to write to the additional queue, violating the decoupling requirement.

questions.question: A financial services firm transfers 4 TB of market-data feeds per day from its co-located on-premises data center to Amazon S3 in us-east-1. The architecture team requires consistent, predictable throughput of at least 1 Gbps. Compliance policy mandates that data must not traverse the public internet. The firm already has a cross-connect available at a colocation facility. Which connectivity solution satisfies all three requirements?
options: AWS Site-to-Site VPN with BGP routing over the corporate internet connection and an AWS-provided certificate
AWS Direct Connect with a 1 Gbps circuit terminating at the colocation cross-connect
AWS Client VPN with split tunneling configured for S3-bound traffic only
S3 Transfer Acceleration routing uploads through CloudFront edge nodes to the target region
questions.explanation: Direct Connect provisions a private physical circuit between the on-premises data center and AWS over the colocation cross-connect, providing guaranteed bandwidth entirely outside the public internet — the only option that simultaneously satisfies the throughput, predictability, and no-public-internet requirements. Site-to-Site VPN is an IPsec tunnel that terminates on public AWS endpoints; even with BGP routing, traffic crosses the public internet, violating the compliance mandate. S3 Transfer Acceleration routes uploads through CloudFront edge locations over the public internet, failing the same requirement and offering no throughput guarantee.

questions.question: A company runs a compliance archival system where regulatory documents are uploaded once and retrieved at most once per year for audits. The compliance team's primary constraint is storage cost, not retrieval speed. Which S3 storage class is most appropriate?
options: S3 Standard — multi-AZ, immediate access, $0.023/GB-month
S3 Standard-IA — millisecond reads, $0.0125/GB-month plus retrieval fee
S3 Glacier Deep Archive — 12-hour retrieval, $0.00099/GB-month
S3 One Zone-IA — single AZ, lower redundancy, millisecond access
questions.explanation: S3 Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost S3 storage class at approximately $0.00099 per GB-month, designed for data accessed at most once or twice per year with a retrieval time of up to 12 hours. For annual compliance audits where retrieval latency is irrelevant, this is the cost-optimal choice. S3 Standard-IA costs more per GB and charges a per-retrieval fee that makes it expensive for unpredictable audit requests; One Zone-IA is cheaper than Standard-IA but more expensive than Glacier and sacrifices multi-AZ durability without offering archival-level pricing.

questions.question: A financial application processes wire transfer instructions from an SQS queue using a Lambda function. After a code deployment, certain message formats cause the Lambda function to throw an unhandled exception. These messages are returned to the queue, immediately retried, and continue failing — consuming Lambda invocations while delaying valid messages. What should the solutions architect implement?
options: Configure a Dead Letter Queue with maxReceiveCount=3 and a depth alarm
Increase the visibility timeout to 5 minutes so Lambda has sufficient time to process each message
Enable FIFO ordering so wire transfers are processed in strict first-in, first-out order
Extend the message retention period to 14 days so failed messages are not permanently deleted
questions.explanation: A Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) receives messages that have exceeded maxReceiveCount processing attempts, permanently removing them from the main queue so they stop consuming Lambda invocations and blocking valid messages. A CloudWatch alarm on DLQ depth alerts the team when failures accumulate, enabling rapid root-cause investigation. Option B (increasing visibility timeout) only delays retries — it does not prevent a 'poison pill' message from cycling through the queue indefinitely once the timeout expires.

questions.question: A horizontally scaled web tier runs across multiple EC2 instances behind an ALB. Users intermittently report being logged out when the ALB routes them to a different instance. Investigation reveals each instance stores session data in local process memory. What is the most operationally simple fix that also survives instance replacement?
options: Enable sticky sessions on the ALB to route each user to the same instance
Move session storage to a shared ElastiCache Redis cluster
Persist each instance's session data to its local EBS volume
Store sessions in DynamoDB and query the session table on each request
questions.explanation: Storing sessions in an external ElastiCache Redis cluster makes session data accessible from any instance in the fleet — a new or replacement instance can immediately retrieve any user's session without interruption, and Multi-AZ mode keeps Redis available even during a primary node failure. Option A (sticky sessions) stops the immediate routing problem but does not fix durability: when the pinned instance is replaced during a deployment or failure, every user session bound to that instance is lost simultaneously, producing a worse batch-logout event than the original complaint.

questions.question: A company needs to migrate 50 TB of data to S3. Their internet connection is 100 Mbps and is needed for business operations. The data must be transferred within 5 days. Which service should they use?
options: AWS DataSync over the existing internet connection
S3 Transfer Acceleration
AWS Snowball Edge
Direct Connect with 1 Gbps port
questions.explanation: 50 TB over 100 Mbps would take approximately 46 days at full utilization. AWS Snowball Edge is a physical device shipped to your location — you load data locally and ship it back to AWS for ingestion into S3, completing the transfer within the 5-day requirement. DataSync and S3 Transfer Acceleration still use the internet connection. Direct Connect provisioning takes weeks.

questions.question: A financial reporting service writes an account balance to DynamoDB and immediately performs a read to return the updated value to the client. Testers consistently observe stale values — the read returns the pre-update balance. The development team wants to fix this in code without changing the table design or data model. What change should they make?
options: Replace GetItem with a Query that uses a FilterExpression on the balance attribute
Set ConsistentRead=true on every GetItem and Query call for this table
Enable DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) for microsecond caching on reads
Switch reads to a Global Secondary Index scoped to the account partition
questions.explanation: Setting ConsistentRead=true forces DynamoDB to read from the partition's leader node and return data that reflects all writes acknowledged before the read, eliminating stale-read windows that exist under eventually consistent (default) mode. DAX caches reads in memory and would worsen the problem — it would serve the cached pre-update value until its TTL expires, not the freshly written value. Global Secondary Indexes do not support strongly consistent reads at all, regardless of the ConsistentRead flag.

questions.question: A media sharing platform lets users upload large video files from a browser. Currently all uploads pass through the application server tier before being written to S3, creating bandwidth bottlenecks and high EC2 costs during peak hours. The security team requires that upload credentials expire no more than 15 minutes after issuance. Which solution removes the application server from the upload data path while meeting the security requirement?
options: Open the S3 bucket for public PUT access and have the browser upload directly
Generate a presigned S3 PUT URL (15-minute TTL) in the application server
Route uploads through an API Gateway integration that proxies the data to S3
Deploy AWS Transfer Family with SFTP to accept browser-based file uploads
questions.explanation: A presigned PUT URL embeds the uploader's identity and an expiry timestamp into a cryptographically signed request URL. The application server generates the URL without touching any file data, then returns it to the browser; the browser PUTs the file directly to S3 — no upload data flows through EC2. Setting the expiry to 15 minutes satisfies the credential lifetime requirement. Option C (API Gateway proxy) replaces the EC2 bottleneck with an API Gateway bottleneck — the full file still transits a server, and API Gateway's 10 MB request body limit makes it unsuitable for large video files.

questions.question: A company has grown to 15 AWS accounts across different business units. The security team requires that all outbound traffic to the internet pass through a single inspection point before leaving AWS. A solutions architect must design the network topology to enforce this without deploying redundant NAT infrastructure in every account. What is the recommended approach?
options: Deploy full-mesh VPC peering between all 15 accounts and route through shared NAT
Attach a Transit Gateway to all accounts with a shared egress VPC at the center
Provision a NAT Gateway in each account and centralize logs in Security Hub
Set up AWS PrivateLink from each spoke account to a centralized proxy service
questions.explanation: AWS Transit Gateway acts as a cloud router connecting all VPCs and accounts. A centralized egress VPC — containing the NAT Gateway and any inspection appliance — is attached to the Transit Gateway, and a default route (0.0.0.0/0) in each spoke's route table directs internet-bound traffic through it. This avoids per-account NAT costs and centralizes egress visibility. Full-mesh VPC peering does not support transitive routing — EC2 in account A cannot reach the internet through a NAT in account B's VPC via peering alone.

questions.question: A company's EC2 instances run in a private subnet with no internet access. The instances need to read objects from an S3 bucket in the same region. The networking team wants to enable this access without deploying a NAT Gateway, which would add hourly charges and route traffic through a public endpoint. What should the engineer configure?
options: Attach an internet gateway to the private subnet and update the route table
Add a route table entry pointing 0.0.0.0/0 at the existing VPC peering connection
Create a Gateway VPC Endpoint for S3 and add a route table entry pointing to it
Move the EC2 instances to a public subnet and configure an S3 bucket policy
questions.explanation: A Gateway VPC Endpoint for S3 is free of charge and injects a managed prefix-list route into the subnet's route table, directing S3-bound traffic through AWS's internal network rather than the internet — satisfying both the no-NAT and no-public-endpoint requirements. An internet gateway cannot be attached to a private subnet; it is a VPC-level resource and still requires a public IP on the instance to function. Moving EC2 instances to a public subnet exposes them to inbound internet traffic and does not eliminate NAT costs when the instances need internet access for other services.

questions.question: A security engineer at a financial services company needs all S3 buckets in the AWS account to have server-side encryption enabled at all times. When a developer creates a bucket without encryption, the configuration must be corrected automatically within minutes — without custom polling scripts. What is the most operationally efficient solution?
options: AWS Config managed rule with an SSM Automation document as the remediation action
Amazon EventBridge rule and a Lambda function that polls S3 bucket settings hourly
AWS Security Hub standard with an automated response and remediation playbook
AWS CloudTrail data events that trigger a Lambda to log non-compliant buckets
questions.explanation: AWS Config evaluates resource configurations in near-real time against managed rules such as s3-bucket-server-side-encryption-enabled. When a rule violation is detected, an automatic remediation action can invoke an SSM Automation document to enable default bucket encryption without any custom code. EventBridge + Lambda polling runs on a schedule, not continuously, so it cannot meet a minutes-level detection requirement and requires custom scripting — which violates the no-polling-scripts constraint. Security Hub aggregates findings but does not natively remediate S3 configurations; CloudTrail data events add cost and still need custom remediation logic.

questions.question: A security engineer is hardening an EC2 web server in a public subnet that requires SSH administration from the corporate network only (CIDR 203.0.113.0/24). All other inbound connections on port 22 must be rejected. The engineer wants the most operationally appropriate AWS-native control. Which configuration achieves this?
options: Add a Network ACL inbound allow rule for TCP 22 from 203.0.113.0/24 with a matching stateless outbound return rule on ephemeral ports
Add an inbound security group rule allowing TCP 22 from source CIDR 203.0.113.0/24
Add iptables rules on the EC2 instance to drop all TCP 22 packets sourced outside 203.0.113.0/24
Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager with an IAM policy restricting access by source IP condition
questions.explanation: Security groups are stateful instance-level firewalls: an inbound allow rule for TCP 22 from 203.0.113.0/24 automatically permits the return traffic without a separate outbound rule, and the rule applies only to the specific instance — the simplest and most targeted control. Network ACLs (option A) are stateless subnet-level firewalls; an inbound allow rule alone is insufficient because a separate explicit outbound rule allowing ephemeral-port return traffic (1024–65535 to 203.0.113.0/24) is also required, and any misconfiguration breaks SSH for all instances in the subnet. iptables (option C) achieves the same result at the OS level but operates outside the AWS control plane, requiring per-instance management with no visibility in VPC flow logs or security group audit trails.

questions.question: A data analytics pipeline ingests hundreds of thousands of events per second from IoT devices. Events need to be processed in real time and stored in S3 for later batch analysis. Which AWS service should anchor the ingestion layer?
options: Amazon SQS Standard Queue
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
Amazon SNS with S3 subscription
Amazon MQ with ActiveMQ
questions.explanation: Kinesis Data Streams is designed for real-time streaming of massive event volumes, supporting hundreds of thousands of records per second per shard. Data can be processed by Kinesis Data Analytics or Lambda in real time while Kinesis Data Firehose delivers a copy to S3. SQS doesn't maintain ordering and isn't designed for real-time analytics pipelines at this scale. SNS doesn't persist data.

questions.question: A healthcare startup stores de-identified patient records in S3. A new compliance framework requires (1) a verifiable log of every encryption key use, and (2) the ability to immediately revoke read access to all stored records during a security incident. The startup uses AWS KMS for key management. Which S3 server-side encryption configuration satisfies both requirements?
options: SSE-S3 using the Amazon-managed S3 key (no KMS dependency)
SSE-KMS with the aws/s3 AWS-managed KMS key for the account
SSE-KMS with a dedicated company-owned KMS key and key policy
Client-side encryption using a key fetched from AWS Secrets Manager
questions.explanation: SSE-KMS with a company-owned KMS key records every GenerateDataKey and Decrypt call in CloudTrail, providing the verifiable key-usage log required by the compliance framework. Disabling the KMS key immediately prevents all future decrypts of every object encrypted with it, satisfying the instant-revoke requirement. Option B (aws/s3 key) also logs KMS events in CloudTrail but is fully managed by AWS — the company cannot disable it, so instant revocation of all read access is not possible.

questions.question: A security audit at a three-tier e-commerce company reveals that the RDS MySQL database security group permits inbound traffic on port 3306 from the entire VPC CIDR (10.0.0.0/16). The auditors require access scoped to only the application EC2 instances. An ALB forwards HTTP to an EC2 app tier, which queries the database. Which security group change satisfies least privilege with no application impact?
options: EC2 SG: inbound 80 from 0.0.0.0/0; RDS SG: inbound 3306 from any VPC instance
EC2 SG: inbound 80 from ALB SG; RDS SG: inbound 3306 from EC2 SG
EC2 SG: inbound 80 from ALB SG; RDS SG: inbound 3306 from 0.0.0.0/0
EC2 SG: inbound all from VPC CIDR; RDS SG: inbound all from VPC CIDR
questions.explanation: Referencing a security group ID in an inbound rule restricts access to exactly those instances carrying that group, updating automatically as instances scale without any IP management. EC2 SG allowing port 80 from the ALB SG accepts traffic only from the load balancer; RDS SG allowing 3306 from the EC2 SG accepts connections only from app instances, not the entire VPC CIDR that the audit flagged. Option A's RDS rule 'from any VPC instance' is functionally equivalent to the original 10.0.0.0/16 CIDR — it still exposes the database to every EC2 instance in the VPC, including developer workstations and unrelated services.

questions.question: A mobile app startup has an existing Cognito User Pool for authentication. The development team is building HTTP endpoints that invoke Lambda functions for business logic — all without maintaining EC2 instances or patching servers. The team wants token validation to happen before Lambda is invoked, with no custom authorizer code to maintain. Which AWS service combination satisfies all three constraints?
options: CloudFront distribution → Lambda@Edge → custom header inspection per edge location
AWS AppSync GraphQL endpoint → Lambda resolvers → Cognito auth provider
API Gateway REST API → Lambda function → Cognito User Pool Authorizer
Application Load Balancer → Lambda target group → Cognito hosted-UI redirect
questions.explanation: API Gateway's native Cognito User Pool Authorizer validates the JWT Bearer token in the Authorization header before routing the request to Lambda — no Lambda Authorizer code to write or maintain. Option D (ALB with Cognito) uses a hosted-UI redirect flow designed for browser OAuth, not a mobile API token flow; the ALB Cognito integration cannot validate pre-issued Bearer tokens inline and instead initiates a browser redirect, which breaks mobile API clients. Option B (AppSync) uses a GraphQL protocol, not the HTTP endpoints the team specified.

questions.question: An operations team at a regional bank runs a critical MySQL database on Amazon RDS in a single Availability Zone. During a DR test, they simulate a hardware failure in the primary AZ — recovery requires a manual restore from a daily snapshot, which takes 45 minutes and requires updating the database connection string in the application. The team's SLA mandates a 5-minute RTO with no application code changes. Which RDS configuration change achieves both requirements?
options: RDS Read Replica promoted manually when the primary instance fails
RDS Multi-AZ with a synchronous standby replica in a second AZ
RDS automated backup with point-in-time recovery to a new instance
RDS Cross-Region Replica with CloudWatch alarm-triggered promotion
questions.explanation: RDS Multi-AZ maintains a synchronous standby that mirrors every committed write from the primary. When the primary AZ becomes unavailable, RDS automatically promotes the standby and updates the DNS CNAME within 60–120 seconds — the application reconnects using the same endpoint with no code changes. Option A (Read Replica) requires a manual promotion step, extending recovery time beyond the 5-minute RTO, and after promotion the application must be updated to use the new endpoint.

questions.question: A company has a global user base. They want to improve performance for users accessing a dynamic API hosted in us-east-1. The API cannot be cached. Which service reduces latency for global users?
options: CloudFront with a custom origin pointing to the API
AWS Global Accelerator with an ALB endpoint in us-east-1
Route 53 latency-based routing to us-east-1
Deploy the API in multiple regions using DynamoDB Global Tables
questions.explanation: AWS Global Accelerator routes user traffic to the AWS global network at the nearest edge location, reducing internet hops and improving TCP/UDP performance for dynamic (uncacheable) content. CloudFront is best for cacheable content. Global Accelerator uses anycast IPs and directs traffic over AWS's optimized backbone. Route 53 latency routing still sends users over the public internet to the origin.

questions.question: A DevOps engineer with full console access accidentally runs `aws cloudformation delete-stack --stack-name prod-infra` during routine maintenance, taking the production environment offline for four hours. The team wants to ensure this cannot happen again without an explicit override step. Which CloudFormation safeguard directly prevents this?
options: Enable termination protection on the stack
CloudFormation drift detection on all stack resources
AWS Config rule monitoring CloudFormation stack events
CloudFormation StackSets for immutable multi-account deployments
questions.explanation: Termination protection causes the delete-stack API call to fail immediately — the request is rejected until an authorized user explicitly disables protection on that stack. This is the simplest direct guard against accidental stack deletion. Drift detection identifies configuration differences between the live resources and the stack definition, but does not block or intercept deletion commands.

questions.question: An application needs to send transactional emails at scale with guaranteed delivery and bounce/complaint handling. Which AWS service is purpose-built for this?
options: Amazon SNS with email subscriptions
Amazon SES (Simple Email Service)
Amazon Pinpoint with email channel
Lambda triggering an SMTP relay on EC2
questions.explanation: Amazon SES is AWS's managed email sending service designed for transactional and marketing email at scale. It handles SMTP, bounce/complaint notifications, dedicated IPs, and email deliverability. SNS email is for notifications/alerts, not transactional emails. Pinpoint is a marketing engagement platform. Self-managing SMTP on EC2 creates unnecessary operational overhead.

questions.question: A company wants to restrict access to an S3 bucket so that only users from a specific AWS Organization can access it, regardless of IAM permissions. Which feature enables this?
options: S3 ACL with an organization-wide condition
S3 bucket policy with aws:PrincipalOrgID condition key
IAM permission boundary applied to all organization users
S3 Block Public Access settings
questions.explanation: The aws:PrincipalOrgID global condition key in an S3 bucket policy allows access only when the principal belongs to the specified AWS Organization. This ensures that even if credentials leak outside the organization, they cannot access the bucket. Permission boundaries apply to individual principals, not organization-wide. S3 Block Public Access blocks anonymous access but not cross-account access.

questions.question: An image-processing service is triggered by S3 uploads and runs on AWS Lambda. High-resolution RAW camera files have started arriving that require 22 minutes of CPU-intensive processing — seven minutes beyond Lambda's hard 15-minute execution limit. The team wants to keep a serverless approach. What is the BEST architectural fix?
options: Lambda at maximum 10 GB memory to reduce CPU execution time
EC2 Auto Scaling group to replace the Lambda function
Step Functions orchestrating chunked Lambda invocations
ECS Fargate task definition to sidestep Lambda time limits
questions.explanation: AWS Step Functions can split a large job into stages — each Lambda invocation processes a chunk of the image within the 15-minute window, and Step Functions manages sequencing, state, and retries. This preserves the serverless model while working around Lambda's hard timeout. Increasing Lambda memory speeds up CPU-bound work but cannot extend the maximum execution limit beyond 15 minutes, so a 22-minute job still fails.

questions.question: A startup operates 50 Lambda functions and an EC2 Auto Scaling group, all of which retrieve database credentials and API keys at startup. The security team requires KMS encryption per value, individual CloudTrail access logging, and version history for rollback. The team must store 500 config values and wants to minimize monthly AWS spend. Which service best meets all three requirements?
options: AWS Secrets Manager — charges $0.40 per secret per month
AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store with SecureString
Amazon S3 with server-side SSE-KMS and object versioning
Amazon DynamoDB table encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key
questions.explanation: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store SecureString parameters are encrypted with KMS, every access call is logged in CloudTrail (including caller identity and parameter name), and each parameter keeps a full version history — all at no charge for the standard tier, making it zero additional cost for 500 values. AWS Secrets Manager also provides encryption and auditing, but charges $0.40 per secret per month — $200/month for 500 secrets. Amazon S3 can store encrypted files but lacks parameter-level access control or native versioning designed for secrets.

questions.question: An e-commerce checkout API runs on an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Flash sale announcements trigger 5× traffic spikes lasting 2-3 minutes, up to 10 times daily at unpredictable times. Cold-starting a new EC2 instance from the AMI takes 4 minutes. Which Auto Scaling configuration absorbs these spikes before they cause user-visible errors?
options: Scheduled scaling actions set to each anticipated spike time
Step scaling combined with a warm pool of stopped instances
Predictive scaling using ML to forecast flash sale demand
Target tracking on ALB RequestCountPerTarget metric
questions.explanation: A warm pool holds pre-initialized EC2 instances in a Stopped state; when the step scaling policy fires, warm pool instances reach InService in seconds rather than the 4-minute cold-start time, so capacity arrives before the 2-3 minute spike ends. Step scaling (rather than simple scaling) adds instances proportional to the alarm breach magnitude, scaling more aggressively when the spike is severe. Scheduled scaling only helps when spike times are predictable, and predictive scaling requires days of historical data before producing a useful forecast.

questions.question: A company's security policy requires that IAM users cannot perform any AWS API action in the current session unless they authenticated with their MFA device — not just their password — during that session. An IAM user who logs in with only username and password must be blocked from all API calls. Which control enforces this at the API request level?
options: IAM password policy set to require MFA device registration
IAM Deny statement on aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent = false
AWS Config managed rule checking MFA activation per user
CloudTrail alarm firing on API calls made without MFA token
questions.explanation: An IAM policy with `Effect: Deny, Action: *` and condition `aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent: false` blocks all API calls in sessions where MFA was not used, regardless of what other policies allow. The user can authenticate but cannot take any action until they use their MFA device. A password policy can require MFA device registration during account setup, but it does not enforce per-request MFA at the API level after login.

questions.question: A company wants to run containerized microservices without managing EC2 instances or clusters, paying only for the resources used by running containers. Which service meets these requirements?
options: Amazon ECS with EC2 launch type
Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate launch type
Amazon EKS with self-managed node groups
Amazon ECR with Auto Scaling
questions.explanation: AWS Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers. With ECS Fargate, you define tasks and services — AWS manages the underlying infrastructure. You pay per vCPU and memory used by running containers, with no EC2 instances to manage, patch, or scale. ECS EC2 launch type requires managing EC2 instances. EKS with self-managed nodes requires managing EC2 nodes. ECR is a container registry, not compute.

questions.question: A company's analytics portal lets users request custom PDF reports that take 8–12 minutes to generate. The architecture must return an immediate acknowledgment to the browser, continue generating the report in the background, and notify the user via SNS when the report is ready. API Gateway has a hard 29-second integration timeout. Which pattern meets all three requirements?
options: Async SQS queue with worker and SNS completion alert
HTTP long-poll connection held open until report finishes
Browser polls a Lambda status endpoint every 10 seconds
API Gateway integration timeout extended past 29 seconds
questions.explanation: An SQS-backed async pattern decouples the browser request from the long-running job: the frontend enqueues the request and immediately receives a job ID, a background worker processes the PDF, and SNS sends a notification on completion. API Gateway's 29-second integration timeout makes options B and D impossible for a task that takes 8–12 minutes — the connection would be terminated before the job finishes. Polling every 10 seconds works but wastes compute and still requires a separate notification mechanism.

questions.question: An Aurora MySQL cluster needs to handle a sudden 10x increase in read traffic due to a promotional campaign. The write workload stays constant. What is the QUICKEST way to scale read capacity?
options: Add more Aurora Read Replicas (up to 15) to the cluster
Promote an existing read replica to become a standalone writer
Enable Aurora Global Database for cross-region reads
Upgrade to a larger DB instance class
questions.explanation: Aurora supports up to 15 read replicas sharing the same underlying storage (unlike RDS replicas which have their own copies). Adding replicas is fast and the cluster reader endpoint automatically distributes reads. Aurora replicas have minimal lag (typically <100ms). Promoting a replica removes read capacity. Global Database adds cross-region latency overhead. Upgrading instance class helps per-replica capacity but doesn't distribute load.

questions.question: A cloud security team must deploy a standard AWS CloudTrail configuration to all 52 accounts in their AWS Organization, including accounts that join the organization in the future. Manually running scripts or console steps per account is not acceptable at this scale. Which AWS service automates this org-wide deployment?
options: Manual CloudFormation stack deployment in each member account
Lambda function calling CreateTrail across member accounts
CloudFormation StackSets with Organizations integration
AWS Config rule alerting when CloudTrail is absent per account
questions.explanation: CloudFormation StackSets with Organizations service-managed permissions automatically deploys and maintains stack instances across all accounts and regions in the organization, including any new account that joins in the future. This requires no per-account scripting. AWS Config can detect missing CloudTrail and raise an alert, but it does not deploy or remediate — it is a detective control, not a preventive or automating one.

questions.question: A fintech company stores payment transactions in DynamoDB. For regulatory compliance, every item modification must be captured in an immutable audit log showing both the old and new attribute values. The solution must not require changes to the existing application, which writes directly to DynamoDB. Which approach creates a complete item-level change history?
options: DynamoDB Point-in-Time Recovery with hourly snapshot comparisons
DynamoDB Streams consumed by Lambda, writing events to S3
DynamoDB on-demand backup job triggered by an EventBridge rule
DynamoDB Global Tables replicating to an audit-only AWS region
questions.explanation: DynamoDB Streams records every INSERT, MODIFY, and REMOVE event at the item level, including both old and new attribute images, with no changes needed in the writing application. A Lambda function triggered by the stream writes each event record to S3, creating an immutable, time-ordered audit trail. Point-in-Time Recovery lets you restore the entire table to a past moment but does not expose a log of individual change events. On-demand backups capture full table snapshots rather than per-modification records, and Global Tables replicate data across regions without tracking what changed.

questions.question: A genomics company runs a batch analysis pipeline on EC2 that processes 3 TB of sequencing data per job, taking 8-12 hours. The pipeline saves progress to S3 every 15 minutes and resumes from the last checkpoint after any failure. Jobs must complete eventually but have no hard deadline. Which EC2 purchasing option minimizes compute cost for this workload?
options: On-Demand Instances billed by the second with no commitment
Spot Instances (up to 90% discount versus On-Demand pricing)
Reserved Instances with a 1-year no-upfront payment plan
Dedicated Hosts reserved for a 1-year term to ensure capacity
questions.explanation: Spot Instances are priced up to 90% below On-Demand rates, and the pipeline's 15-minute checkpointing makes it tolerant of the 2-minute Spot interruption notice — if the instance is reclaimed, the job restarts from the last S3 checkpoint with minimal rework. Dedicated Hosts are reserved physical servers intended for software licensing compliance and are the most expensive per-hour option. Reserved Instances reduce costs for predictable, steady-state workloads but are poorly suited to intermittent jobs that only run when triggered.

questions.question: A SaaS company wants to enforce HTTPS on its public web application. Users who access the plain HTTP URL in their browser should automatically be sent to the HTTPS version. The change must be applied at the load balancer with no modifications to the application servers. Which load balancer type and configuration achieves this?
options: Network Load Balancer with port forwarding from TCP 80 to TCP 443
Application Load Balancer with an HTTP listener redirect action
Classic Load Balancer with an HTTP listener and SSL offloading
Gateway Load Balancer with inline traffic forwarding rules
questions.explanation: Application Load Balancer (ALB) is the only AWS load balancer that can inspect Layer-7 HTTP content and respond with a redirect action — for example, returning an HTTP 301 on port 80 that points the browser to the HTTPS endpoint on port 443. This is configured as a listener rule on the port-80 listener and involves no backend instances. Network Load Balancer operates at Layer 4 (TCP) and cannot read or modify HTTP headers, so it cannot issue a protocol-level redirect. Classic Load Balancer supports SSL termination but lacks listener rule actions for automatic HTTP-to-HTTPS promotion.

questions.question: A bank's compliance team must ensure that API audit logs shipped to an S3 bucket cannot be modified or deleted by anyone — including administrators and the root account — before a mandatory 90-day hold expires. They also need cryptographic proof that each log file has not been altered since delivery. Which two controls together satisfy both requirements?
options: Enable S3 MFA Delete and turn on bucket versioning for the log bucket
Enable log file validation and apply S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode
Encrypt logs with a KMS CMK and restrict key usage to the security team
Add a bucket policy Deny on s3:DeleteObject for all IAM principals
questions.explanation: S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode creates a WORM hold that even the root account cannot override before the retention period ends, satisfying the deletion-prevention requirement. CloudTrail log file validation generates an hourly SHA-256 digest chain; any post-delivery tampering breaks the chain and is immediately detectable, providing the cryptographic integrity proof. KMS encryption (option C) protects confidentiality but not integrity — an administrator with key access could still delete the objects. MFA Delete (option A) can be disabled by the root user, so it does not provide the same ironclad guarantee as Object Lock Compliance mode.

questions.question: A company's e-commerce platform is fully stateless and handles flash sales that spike traffic to 10× normal within 30 seconds. The infrastructure team cannot reliably pre-warm capacity for unpredictable sale windows. Which compute approach meets the sub-minute scaling requirement?
options: EC2 Auto Scaling with target-tracking scaling on CPU
AWS Lambda behind an Application Load Balancer
A pre-sized On-Demand EC2 fleet reserved for peak load
Elastic Beanstalk with time-based scheduled scale-out
questions.explanation: AWS Lambda scales from zero to thousands of concurrent executions in seconds without provisioning or warm-up delays, making it ideal for unpredictable sub-minute traffic spikes. EC2 Auto Scaling typically takes 3–5 minutes to launch and initialize new instances — far too slow for a 30-second surge. Pre-sizing an EC2 fleet covers the spike but wastes cost during normal load, and Elastic Beanstalk time-based scaling requires predicting when surges occur.

questions.question: A financial company's on-premises Oracle 19c database is written to 24/7 and must be migrated to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with fewer than 4 hours of application downtime. The database is 2 TB. Which migration approach satisfies this requirement?
options: AWS DMS with CDC replication to Aurora PostgreSQL
Oracle Data Pump with a scheduled maintenance window
AWS Snowball physical transfer for the 2 TB export
AWS SCT schema conversion running as standalone migration
questions.explanation: AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) performs a full initial load, then uses Change Data Capture (CDC) to replicate ongoing transactions to the Aurora target while the Oracle source remains online — shrinking the cutover window to minutes. Oracle Data Pump requires pausing writes during export, which cannot meet a 4-hour constraint for a 2 TB actively-written database. AWS Snowball handles bulk data transport but provides no mechanism for live replication. AWS Schema Conversion Tool converts schemas and code objects but does not migrate data on its own.

questions.question: An enterprise manages a central networking account containing a VPC with carefully segmented subnets. Twenty application accounts in the same AWS Organization need to deploy EC2 instances and RDS clusters using those centrally managed subnets, without owning their own VPCs. Which AWS capability enables this?
options: AWS Resource Access Manager shared subnets
AWS Transit Gateway with cross-account attachments
VPC Peering from the hub account to each spoke
AWS PrivateLink endpoint services per spoke VPC
questions.explanation: AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) lets the subnet-owning account share specific subnets with participant accounts in the same AWS Organization. Participants can launch EC2, RDS, and other resources directly into those shared subnets while the network team retains control of routing, NACLs, and security groups. AWS Transit Gateway interconnects separate VPCs at the routing level but does not let participant accounts deploy into a single shared subnet. VPC Peering links two separate VPCs without granting subnet-level access to a participant account. PrivateLink exposes specific services, not shared network segments.

questions.question: A SaaS provider runs a payment-processing API inside their AWS VPC. A customer company wants to invoke that API from within their own VPC without traversing the internet, without CIDR overlap constraints, and without gaining access to any other resource in the provider's VPC. Which networking pattern satisfies all three requirements?
options: AWS PrivateLink backed by a Network Load Balancer
VPC Peering between provider and customer accounts
AWS Transit Gateway connecting both company VPCs
AWS Direct Connect dedicated link to the provider
questions.explanation: AWS PrivateLink creates an Interface VPC Endpoint in the consumer's VPC that maps to a VPC Endpoint Service backed by a Network Load Balancer in the provider's VPC. Traffic stays within the AWS network, CIDR ranges never conflict, and the consumer can only reach that specific NLB — not the rest of the provider's VPC. VPC Peering and Transit Gateway grant full network-level access across VPCs, violating the isolation requirement. AWS Direct Connect is designed for on-premises-to-AWS private connectivity, not for inter-VPC API-level service sharing.

questions.question: A team's serverless checkout API runs on API Gateway backed by Lambda. During a flash sale, multiple functions in the same AWS account exhaust the shared regional concurrency pool, leaving the checkout function throttled while lower-priority background functions remain active. The team wants to guarantee the checkout function always has a minimum concurrency allocation that other functions in the account cannot claim. Which Lambda feature addresses this?
options: Provisioned concurrency for the checkout Lambda function
Reserved concurrency set on the checkout Lambda function
AWS Lambda Power Tuning to reduce per-invocation duration
API Gateway usage plan throttling per customer API key
questions.explanation: Reserved concurrency carves out a dedicated slice of the account-level concurrency pool exclusively for the specified function. Other functions cannot consume that reserved portion, ensuring the checkout function is never starved by lower-priority workloads competing for the shared pool. Provisioned concurrency (option A) pre-initializes execution environments to eliminate cold starts and improve latency, but it does not prevent other functions from consuming the unreserved portion of the account-wide limit that applies to non-provisioned invocations. API Gateway usage plans throttle individual external callers but have no effect on how Lambda allocates its internal concurrency pool.

questions.question: A data engineering team stores 18 months of clickstream logs in Amazon S3 as Parquet files partitioned by date. Business analysts need to run ad-hoc SQL queries against this data without provisioning a database cluster or building ETL pipelines. Which service meets this need at the lowest operational overhead?
options: Amazon Athena querying via the Glue Data Catalog
Amazon Redshift Spectrum reading S3 Parquet directly
Amazon EMR Spark cluster querying the S3 dataset
AWS Glue Studio ETL job loading S3 data to DynamoDB
questions.explanation: Amazon Athena is fully serverless — analysts write standard SQL and Athena reads Parquet files directly from S3 using the Glue Data Catalog for schema and partition information, with no cluster to provision or maintain. Amazon Redshift Spectrum also queries S3 directly but requires a running Redshift cluster, adding provisioning overhead. Amazon EMR provides distributed processing power but requires launching and managing a cluster. AWS Glue Studio is a data transformation tool that writes data to a target store — it does not provide an ad-hoc SQL query interface.

questions.question: A company uses IAM Identity Center (SSO). An audit requirement mandates that all administrative actions in all AWS accounts must be logged with the caller's identity. Which service provides this centrally?
options: AWS Config aggregator across all accounts
AWS CloudTrail Organization Trail writing to a central S3 bucket in a log archive account
Amazon CloudWatch Logs cross-account subscription
VPC Flow Logs from all accounts sent to S3
questions.explanation: An AWS CloudTrail Organization Trail automatically enables CloudTrail in all accounts in the organization, with all events delivered to a central S3 bucket in a log archive account. This creates an immutable, centralized audit log of all API activity including the IAM Identity Center caller identity. Config aggregates configuration state, not API call logs. VPC Flow Logs capture network traffic, not API calls.

questions.question: A fintech company's SOC 2 audit requires that third-party auditors, who operate their own separate AWS account, have read-only access to specific S3 buckets for a two-week review window. The security team's constraints are: no long-lived credentials may be created, and no bucket endpoint may be exposed to the public internet. What should they configure?
options: Create an IAM user per auditor and email the access keys to each
Create a cross-account IAM role and share the role ARN for assumption
Share presigned S3 URLs (2-week expiry) directly with each auditor
Create a new AWS account for auditors and assign root-level S3 access
questions.explanation: A cross-account IAM role with an S3 read-only policy and a trust policy scoped to the auditor's AWS account lets the auditors call sts:AssumeRole to obtain short-lived temporary credentials — no long-lived keys are created or shared. Deleting the role at the end of the review instantly revokes all access. Sharing IAM user access keys by email (option A) creates long-lived credentials that may be forwarded or cached, violating the no-permanent-credentials requirement. Presigned URLs (option C) are internet-accessible HTTPS endpoints — anyone who holds the URL can fetch the object — and cannot be scoped to another AWS account's identity, failing both security constraints.

questions.question: An application reads configuration from Parameter Store at startup and restarts frequently, causing high API call volume and throttling. What should the solutions architect recommend?
options: Switch to environment variables stored in EC2 User Data
Use AWS AppConfig with a caching client, or implement parameter caching in the application
Upgrade Parameter Store to Advanced tier for higher throughput
Move all parameters to S3 and read from there
questions.explanation: AWS AppConfig is built for application configuration with native client-side caching and validation. For Parameter Store, implementing a cache (cache parameters at startup for 5-10 minutes) dramatically reduces GetParameter API calls. The Advanced tier increases throughput limits but adds cost — caching is free and more architecturally sound. Reading from S3 lacks versioning, encryption, and audit features of Parameter Store.

questions.question: A media company needs to transcode uploaded videos into multiple formats. Jobs take 5-20 minutes each and thousands of videos are uploaded daily. Which architecture is MOST scalable and cost-effective?
options: A single large EC2 instance running transcoding software
S3 upload event triggers Lambda, but Lambda cannot handle 20-minute jobs without Step Functions
S3 upload event to SQS queue consumed by ECS Fargate tasks that auto-scale based on queue depth
Store videos in EFS and batch process with a Glue ETL job
questions.explanation: S3 event → SQS → ECS Fargate with auto-scaling based on queue depth is the ideal pattern for long-running batch jobs. Fargate tasks pick up jobs from SQS, process them (no Lambda 15-minute limit), and scale out as the queue grows. Fargate is serverless — no EC2 management. A single EC2 creates a bottleneck. Lambda can't handle 20-minute jobs reliably. EFS/Glue doesn't leverage the event-driven pattern.

questions.question: A company needs to protect an ALB-fronted web application from SQL injection and XSS attacks. Which service provides this protection at the load balancer level?
options: AWS Shield Standard
Security Groups on the ALB
AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall) attached to the ALB
Amazon GuardDuty
questions.explanation: AWS WAF operates at Layer 7 and can inspect HTTP request content (body, headers, URI) for SQL injection and XSS patterns using AWS Managed Rules or custom rules. WAF can be attached directly to ALB, CloudFront, or API Gateway. Shield Standard protects against DDoS volumetric attacks at Layers 3/4, not application-layer attacks. Security Groups are Layer 4. GuardDuty is threat detection, not a blocking WAF.

questions.question: A three-tier e-commerce application runs web servers, app servers, and an RDS MySQL database in separate subnets. A security audit finds the RDS instance accepts connections on port 3306 from the full VPC CIDR (10.0.0.0/16). The team must restrict database access to only the app-tier EC2 instances in a way that remains accurate as instances are replaced or the fleet scales without manual IP updates. What should they configure?
options: Update the RDS security group to allow port 3306 from the app subnet CIDR
Reference the app-tier security group in the RDS security group inbound rule
Apply a subnet NACL on the RDS subnet blocking all traffic except from the app subnet
Move the RDS instance to an isolated VPC connected to the app tier via PrivateLink
questions.explanation: Referencing a security group ID in an inbound rule grants access to all instances carrying that group at the time of each request — when app-tier instances are replaced or scale out, new EC2s inherit the security group and immediately gain database access without any manual rule update. Restricting to the app subnet CIDR (option A) allows any EC2 in that subnet — monitoring agents, developer tools, or a compromised instance — not just the app-tier application, violating least-privilege isolation. NACLs (option C) are stateless: an inbound allow for port 3306 also requires an explicit outbound rule covering ephemeral reply ports (1024–65535), doubling maintenance overhead and increasing the chance of misconfiguration that locks out valid traffic.

questions.question: A company wants to run analytics queries on petabytes of structured data with complex JOINs requiring sub-minute response times. Which AWS service is DESIGNED for this workload?
options: Amazon DynamoDB with GSIs
Amazon Athena with S3 data lake
Amazon Redshift
Amazon RDS Aurora with read replicas
questions.explanation: Amazon Redshift is a petabyte-scale columnar data warehouse optimized for complex analytical queries (OLAP) with massive parallel processing (MPP). It handles complex JOINs and aggregations over billions of rows far more efficiently than row-based databases. DynamoDB excels at low-latency single-item access. Athena is good for ad-hoc queries but slower at this scale. RDS is OLTP, not OLAP.

questions.question: An application on EC2 has an IAM role with s3:* and ec2:* permissions. The application only reads from one specific S3 bucket. What change enforces least privilege?
options: Add a Deny policy for all other services
Remove ec2:* entirely and replace s3:* with s3:GetObject restricted to the specific bucket ARN
Move the permissions to an IAM user attached to the instance
Add a condition key restricting actions by source IP
questions.explanation: Least privilege means granting only the exact permissions required. Replace s3:* with s3:GetObject on the specific bucket ARN (arn:aws:s3:::bucket-name/*) and remove ec2:* entirely since the application doesn't need EC2 API calls. This minimizes blast radius if the instance is compromised. Using a Deny policy on top of broad Allow is less clean than not granting the permissions. IAM users on EC2 is an anti-pattern.

questions.question: A company has an active-passive DR setup across two AWS regions. The RTO is 15 minutes and RPO is 1 minute. Which database replication approach meets the RPO requirement?
options: Daily RDS snapshots copied to the secondary region
RDS cross-region read replica with replication lag under 1 minute
Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) with 1-minute granularity
Amazon Aurora Global Database with typical replication lag under 1 second
questions.explanation: Aurora Global Database provides cross-region replication with typical lag under 1 second (well within 1-minute RPO). In a disaster, the secondary region can be promoted in under 1 minute (within RTO). Standard RDS cross-region replicas have higher lag and slower promotion. Daily snapshots produce RPO of up to 24 hours. PITR restoration itself takes minutes to hours.

questions.question: A company needs to access AWS service APIs (SSM, EC2 API, STS) from private subnets without routing traffic over the internet. Which is the CORRECT solution?
options: Deploy a NAT Gateway for all AWS API traffic
Create Interface VPC Endpoints (powered by AWS PrivateLink) for the required AWS services
Use Gateway Endpoints for all AWS services
Set up a bastion host to proxy all AWS API calls
questions.explanation: Interface VPC Endpoints create elastic network interfaces (ENIs) in your subnet that provide private access to AWS service APIs via AWS PrivateLink — no internet, no NAT required. Gateway Endpoints exist only for S3 and DynamoDB (free). Interface endpoints cover most other AWS services (hourly charge + data processing fee). NAT Gateway routes traffic over the internet and incurs higher data transfer costs.

questions.question: A financial services firm must satisfy a compliance mandate that all AWS API activity — including read-only calls — be retained for 7 years with cryptographic proof that no log has been altered or deleted after delivery. The team routes logs to a dedicated S3 archive bucket. Which combination of CloudTrail and S3 settings satisfies all three requirements?
options: Log file validation enabled; S3 Standard storage with a 7-year lifecycle rule
Log file validation enabled; S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode (7-year hold)
KMS CMK encryption; S3 Glacier Deep Archive with a 7-year expiry policy
MFA Delete and S3 versioning enabled; S3 Standard-IA with a 7-year lifecycle rule
questions.explanation: CloudTrail log file validation generates an hourly SHA-256 digest chain; any modification to a log file or its digest after delivery breaks the chain, providing cryptographic proof of integrity. S3 Object Lock in Compliance mode creates a WORM hold for the full retention period that even the root account cannot override, guaranteeing 7-year immutability and satisfying the tamper-proof requirement. Option A enables log file validation but stores objects in S3 Standard without Object Lock — an administrator can still delete the files, failing the deletion-prevention requirement. KMS encryption (option C) protects confidentiality but not integrity; a user with key access could still delete objects. MFA Delete (option D) can be disabled by the root account and does not provide the same ironclad protection as Object Lock Compliance mode.

questions.question: A company is migrating a monolith to microservices on AWS. Services need to communicate synchronously with low latency. Which AWS service is BEST for synchronous inter-service HTTP communication?
options: Amazon SQS for all service-to-service calls
Amazon SNS for broadcasting requests
Amazon API Gateway (HTTP APIs) or ALB for service-to-service HTTP/HTTPS calls
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams for all inter-service messaging
questions.explanation: Synchronous inter-service communication requires request-response semantics. API Gateway HTTP APIs (lower latency, lower cost than REST APIs) or ALB with path-based routing to different microservices is the standard AWS pattern. API Gateway adds authentication, throttling, and request transformation. ALB is simpler for internal traffic. SQS and Kinesis are asynchronous. SNS is a pub/sub broadcast system.
